subject: Recap: SproutPay compliance discovery + evidence asks and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sproutpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: SproutPay compliance discovery + evidence asks and next steps

Tom / Lena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track asks.

High-level goals you shared:
- Go-live for initial integration (inbound routing + embeddings search) by early November 2027.
- Meet your procurement/compliance gating: SOC 2 (in-scope controls for logs/audit), DPA signed, evidence for retention and pen-test results.

Primary pain points we heard:
1) Audit logging: you need proof of immutable audit logs for admin actions and a retention policy that supports investigations (suggested 3+ years, legal to confirm).
2) Data residency / retention: requirement to retain transaction metadata for a longer window for regulators, plus a second-tier archive.
3) Pen test / vulnerability evidence: internal procurement requires pen-test report or sign-off, and a list of remediation cadence.
4) DPA & MPA terms: legal needs standard EU/US DPA with explicit subprocessor list and deletion/retention clauses.

Immediate asks (I’ve attached a short DDQ that covers the items we discussed): sproutpay-internal-ddq-asks.pdf
- We will populate and return an evidence matrix by EOD Thu, June 10 (items: SOC 2 scope, audit log retention paths, sample log snippet, encryption at rest/in-transit docs).
- Please confirm target retention window (you mentioned 3 vs 7 years) and whether archived cold storage is acceptable for >3y.
- Confirm pen-test timing: you said internal vendor window in August — is Red-Team report acceptable or do you require 3rd-party audit?

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood sends completed evidence matrix (by 2027-06-10). Attachment: redwood-evidence-matrix.xlsx.
2) Schedule security deep-dive (technical) with Karthik + infra on Wed June 17 (30–45m).
3) Legal teams start DPA exchange; we’ll share a draft DPA + sample SOW by next week.

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update. Thanks — appreciate the clarity on timelines.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sproutpay-internal-ddq-asks.pdf (10 pages, DDQ with prioritized asks)
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sproutpay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@sproutpay.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: SproutPay compliance discovery + evidence asks and next steps

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: our legal team prefers a 3-year hot/online retention with an optional cold archive up to 7 years for compliance investigations. If archive is cold with restricted access that should be fine.
- SOC 2: we are in the middle of Type II readiness; auditor kickoff is planned for late Q3 (Sept). We can share your SOC 2 attestation once available but procurement needs interim controls evidence now (logs, access review cadence, encryption details).
- Pen test: we normally accept a vendor-conducted 3rd-party pen test. Our internal team is also doing a limited “red-team” in August — ideally we’d have Redwood’s most recent public pen-test report or a letter summarizing recent security assessments.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood supports: 1) exportable audit logs on request (JSON/CSV), and 2) customer-managed KMS for key separation? Those are gating items for our security review.

Appreciate the timeline — please share the evidence matrix and we’ll respond with any follow-up items.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Infrastructure Security, SproutPay
Tom.Reynolds@sproutpay.com | +1 (617) 555-4092

Subject: Re: Recap: SproutPay compliance discovery + evidence asks and next steps

Hi Tom / Lena — Marissa here (Solutions). Follows on the technical side and what we’ll include in the evidence matrix (redwood-evidence-matrix.xlsx attached):

Quick answers up front:
- Audit logs: yes — we can provide exportable logs (JSON) for admin events, model invocation metadata, and retention metadata. We’ll include a redacted sample log snippet in the matrix.
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS / HSM integrations) for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS for Enterprise customers.

What I’ll include in the matrix (and expected delivery):
1) Sample log schema + redacted sample (admin events, request IDs, timestamps).
2) Retention architecture: short-term hot storage (90 days), medium (3 years, online), long-term cold archive (optional up to 7 years).
3) Pen-test evidence options: recent public pen-test summary + criteria for bespoke 3rd-party tests for Dedicated customers.
4) DPA items: subprocessor list, data deletion pathways, and the default retention policy language we typically propose.

Proposed near-term schedule:
- 2027-06-10 EOD: upload evidence matrix and sample artifacts to shared Drive link.
- 2027-06-17 11:00am PT: security deep-dive (Karthik + infra + Tom team). Please confirm if that slot works.
- Following deep-dive: prepare DPA draft and SOW for review (target: 2027-06-24).

Attachment: redwood-evidence-matrix.xlsx (live tracker)

Thanks — I’ll upload the matrix this week and add a short readme so your procurement can triage items quickly.

—Marissa

Tom / Lena — Karthik (Security) stepping in to confirm a couple practical items ahead of the deep-dive:

1) Pen-test: we can share our latest 3rd-party pen-test summary (redacted) and offer a scoped assessment for Dedicated deployments if you require an on-prem-style full test. For hosted customers we frequently provide a signed security attestation and recent CVE remediation timeline.
2) Logs & export: exportable logs (JSON/CSV) are supported; for high-volume export we can provide streaming export to a customer-owned S3 bucket as part of Dedicated/Private setups.

I’ll bring the sample attestation and our evidence playbook to the June 17 call. If you confirm the slot, I’ll include an internal checklist so procurement can mark items as satisfied/needs follow-up.

—Karthik
